findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext drops logs, and the moved logging attributes have no tests
findings.body: `FromContext` returns a fresh `NewTestLogger()`. Anything logged through it is recorded on an object the test never sees. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs only through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go:58). So if a test injects a `*TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and then checks `InfoLogs`, it will always see zero calls, and its assertions will either fail or pass without checking anything. No test does this today, but that also means nothing checks that the "Plugin Request Completed" line still carries `pluginId`/`endpoint`/`dsUID`/`uname`/`traceID` now that those come from the context instead of being added explicitly. Consider returning `f` from `FromContext` so logs still reach the test, and adding a test that chains `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` and `LoggerMiddleware`.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware now emits "Plugin Request Completed" through m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of explicitly adding pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: the same attributes were added inline in logRequest. Now ContextualLoggerMiddleware puts pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname into the context, and the tracing package's registered provider adds traceID.
contracts.before_after: ContextualLoggerMiddleware sits directly before LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares, and TracingMiddleware comes before both, so the context carries the attributes and a span when logRequest runs. ConcreteLogger.FromContext collects all providers' args and calls cl.New(args...), which keeps the base "logger" key.
contracts.visible_effect: The log line keeps the same keys (in a different order). It also picks up attributes from any other registered provider, such as ngalert's rule key.
contracts.failure_mode: If no provider returns args, FromContext returns the logger unchanged. The attributes are lost only if LoggerMiddleware is ever wired without ContextualLoggerMiddleware before it; today there is a single wiring site.

contracts.equivalent_path: The former instrumentContext call inside InstrumentationMiddleware.instrumentPluginRequest, made right before fn(ctx)
contracts.before_after: Before, the context was enriched inside the metrics middleware, after pluginTarget succeeded. Now it is enriched in the next middleware. If pluginTarget fails, the metrics middleware still returns before reaching it, so nothing downstream runs in either version. The metrics middleware itself does not log with the context, so every logger downstream sees the same attributes as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Downstream plugin-related logs carry the same attributes as before.
contracts.failure_mode: Synchronous context wrapping with no error path. Stream methods pass through without enrichment, same as before.

contracts.action: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts the result of ConcreteLogger.FromContext to *log.ConcreteLogger
contracts.before_after: ConcreteLogger.FromContext returns either cl.New(args...) or cl, both of type *ConcreteLogger, so the assertion always succeeds.
contracts.visible_effect: The wrapped logger keeps the "logger" name and adds the context attributes.
contracts.failure_mode: The `!ok` fallback (d.New()) cannot be reached with the current infra implementation.

summary:
I found no defects. The refactor keeps the plugin request log lines and the context attributes the same, with one optional test suggestion.

- **Log content:** the "Plugin Request Completed" line keeps the same fields: `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` and `traceID`. These now come from the context instead of being added in the logger middleware itself. The new contextual logger middleware runs right before the logger middleware, and the tracing middleware runs first, so the span is there to supply `traceID` (pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91).
- **Downstream logs:** they get the same attributes as before. The metrics middleware, which now runs ahead of the step that adds them, doesn't log with the context. When the plugin isn't registered, both versions stop before any downstream middleware runs.
- **New `FromContext` on the plugin logger:** its type check always succeeds, because the infra logger always returns that concrete type, so the fallback branch can't run.
- **Interface change:** `Logger` has only two implementations, the real wrapper and `TestLogger`. Both now have the new method, so nothing else breaks.

One "consider" (tests): `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a fresh logger, so a test that checks the logger middleware's output would never see its log line. Nothing currently checks that the moved fields still appear in that line.

One dependency to keep in mind: the logger middleware now relies on the contextual logger middleware being placed before it. Today that ordering is set in one place, `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginsintegration.go`.
